title: Opening, birth and childhood neighborhood
summary: Dick Allen opens the session (July 10, 1961, at Bill Russell's home). Chester Jones says he was born at Cutoff and lived all his life around St. Philip Street near the Caledonia.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Let me put a little something on here first. We're recording today at 731 St. Peter, Bill Russell's home in Rekacha. Let's see, what's today's date? July... Is it the 10th? I think it's the 10th. It's Monday anyway. Yeah, the 10th. July the 10th, 1961. And what's your name? Chester Jones. Chester Jones. And my name is Dick Allen. Let's see. I guess I've known you about 11 years now, but we might as well go back long before that. Oh, yeah. Might as well start at the beginning. Yeah. Where were you born? I think I was born in Cutoff, Louisiana. That's low-coast Al Jays.

Down the river, in other words, on the other side. That's right. Well, I left there. Parents said they'd take me from here when I was a year old. Stayed at 1115 St. Phil Street. I was stood there for about 15 to 20 years or maybe better. Left there and we moved down in the night war down on Law Street. Bought a home down there. Still there for a while. They'd come back to the same old house again. I don't know if it's at St. Phil but 15th, 1115 St. Phil Street. Stood there again about, I'd say about 10 years. Then we moved to 1325 Duman Street. All around the same neighborhood. Right around the same vicinity. Been around that neighborhood all my days. Right around St. Phil Street. Right around the, uh, that's near where the Caledonia Club is. Yeah, all right around that same neighborhood. Well, I was staying in the block of Caledonia. Mm-hmm. In fact, I was staying there when there was a grocery and a ballroom and people that owned the building today. Well, the mother's dead, the father's dead, and a couple of the sons are living that owns that building. Tessitory family. We were probably raised up together as far as Tessitory. They even had some wakes in there. Oh yeah, a father by the name of Clarence Blanchett, they waked him in there. And, uh, let's see now. I can recall back. Trying to think of who the other fellow that waked him there. I think a father by the name of Richard Martin, I think he was waked in there too. We played both of the fields right from there. Mm-hmm. Well, how'd they have them laid out in there? Well, it's a place they have in the back where they used to use for store room. Mm-hmm. They cleaned that room out of later, took everything out of there, put benches back there, chairs back there for the people to settle in there. Had enough space to lay the body. Had quite a number of people at the wake too. I'd say closer on four to five hundred people at the wake.
